chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The human being has more right to his wealth as long as the soul remains in his body.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to control one's wealth during their lifetime according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*’s chapter on revoking wills, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the absolute autonomy of the living owner over their assets, providing the foundational justification for the legal permissibility of *ruju'* (revocation) before death. It highlights that the transfer of wealth upon death is a distinct legal event, whereas lifetime possession is governed by the individual's immediate will and capacity. This principle reinforces the Shia juristic view that the living owner is the primary authority in disposing of their property, whether through gift, sale, or bequest.
